title: Honest selection under many attempts, the library's part: a selection fold read once and the measured optimism (34.6)
request: The owner asked to finish Phase 10 without stopping. The plan (docs/guides/PHASE10_ABILITIES_PLAN.md, 34.6, the MLE plan's 33.2) asks for a selection protocol fixed before any wider search: search folds and a selection fold, the measured optimism in the record.
spec: dclab_core/selection.py: selection_split (cut as the project splits), choose (the winner on the search rows read once on the selection fold) and SelectionRecord v1; measured on simulated candidates of known quality before the engine uses it.
plan: read the MLE plan's 33.2 and the engine's selection
write the selection split and the choice with its record
simulate candidates of about equal true quality and measure each rule's optimism against a holdout
choose the default from the measurement, register the contract and its schema

decisions.decision: Confirm only the winner on the selection fold by default
decisions.why: measured: choosing among three there carries that choice's own luck, larger than plain cross-validation's at five attempts; confirming one keeps the score honest at every count

decisions.decision: The library scores nothing itself: the host passes a function that scores a candidate on the selection fold
decisions.why: the engine and the main product fit their own models; the protocol is the same for both

decisions.decision: Wire it into the engine together with the wider search of 34.7
decisions.why: today's engine tries a handful of candidates; setting rows aside costs every project training rows for little gain until the search widens

change: dclab_core/selection.py (new: selection_split, choose, SelectionRecord v1); dclab_core/contracts.py and adapters/conformance.py (registered); schemas; version 0.110.0 and CHANGELOG; CORE_INTEGRATION.md section; tests/test_core_selection.py (new).

findings.defect: choosing among the top three on the selection fold reported a flattered score
findings.scenario: simulated candidates with search noise smaller than the selection fold's: the chosen one's selection score beat its holdout by about 0.025 at every number of attempts, more than plain cross-validation's winner at five attempts
findings.cause: the best of three noisy readings holds the luck of that choice, as the best of many search scores does
findings.fix: the default confirms only the winner; with more than one, the record says to read the score as an upper estimate
findings.impact: an honest-looking score that is not, the very fault the protocol is for
alternatives: a third split to score the chosen one: fewer rows for each part on small tables

measurements.name: optimism by number of attempts, simulated candidates (400 searches each)
measurements.gate: plain cross-validation's optimism grows with attempts; the protocol's default stays near zero at every count
measurements.result: plain 0.019, 0.039 and 0.051 at 5, 50 and 200 attempts; confirming the winner 0.002, -0.003 and 0.002; choosing among three 0.024, 0.023 and 0.027
measurements.next: measure on the replicas with planted noise through the engine with 34.7
limits: simulated scores, not models fitted on tables
one noise level for each reading

outcome: DCLab has the selection protocol a wide search needs: a fold set aside before it, read once for the winner, with the measured optimism in a versioned record; the engine uses it with 34.7.
lessons: Measure a protocol against the fault it is for before choosing its default: the obvious choice among three repeated the fault.
A fold used to choose is no longer a fold that can tell the truth about the choice.
risks: a selection fold takes training rows from every search
small tables give a selection fold too noisy to confirm anything
